Gala apple: growing Gale Gala, Redlum Gala and Gala Venus in India

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Gala strains such as Gale Gala, Redlum Gala and Gala Venus are bright red, early apples harvested in July–August. They need 700–1,000 chilling hours and work both as a main variety and as a pollinizer for Delicious (Himachal package of practices).

Gala
Tree habit and fruitStandard; bright early red
Chilling need700–1,000 hours below 7°C
Role in the orchardBoth a main variety and a pollinizer
StrengthsEarly harvest in July–August with export-grade fruit; doubles as a pollinizer for Delicious.
WeaknessesFruit is smaller at the highest elevations.

Because Gala ripens 110–120 days after full bloom, against 130–145 for Delicious, it reaches the market before the main Delicious glut. Redlum Gala is one of the recommended diploid pollinizers, so a Gala row inside a Delicious block does two jobs.

Rootstock, spacing and feeding

Choose the rootstock by soil, not by variety alone: M.9 only on deep, fertile, irrigated land with a trellis; MM.106 only on well-drained soil; MM.111 on drier slopes (rootstock guide). Feed by tree age with our apple fertilizer calculator.

Pollination

Keep 25–33% compatible pollinizers flowering at the same time, 4–6 beehives per hectare at bloom, a boron spray at pink bud, and no sprays during full bloom.

Compare: all apple varieties and rootstocks.

Questions farmers ask

How much chilling does Gala need?

700–1,000 hours below 7°C.

Does Gala need a pollinizer?

Both a main variety and a pollinizer.

What are the problems with Gala?

Fruit is smaller at the highest elevations.
